title: Orange and rhubarb compote with yoghurt

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oranges, rhubarb, honey, oats, almonds, natural yoghurt and cinnamon are all whole, home-kept foods.

supermarket.reason: Tesco stocks forced rhubarb in January alongside oranges, oats, almonds and yoghurt at everyday prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a grater, a knife, a saucepan and a frying pan, and peeling oranges into rounds is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 400g rhubarb simmered with orange juice and honey for 5 minutes, served over 500g yoghurt with toasted oats and almonds, makes a sensible four portions that will be soft, sweet enough and not watery.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers zesting and peeling four oranges, cutting the rhubarb, chopping the almonds and watching the toasting pan, and the 8 minutes of cooking matches the 5-minute simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon are used in the steps, nothing unlisted appears, and each name matches its id.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm compote of oranges with early forced rhubarb suits early January, and the oranges supply the zest, the juice and the slices, so they are central.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour would follow without trouble.

hearty_healthy.reason: Yoghurt, fruit, oats and nuts make a balanced breakfast with protein and fibre and only modest added honey.
